articles.title: How Rocky Became the Heart of Philadelphia
articles.summary: Fifty years after Rocky brought the City of Brotherly Love to the big screen, the fictional boxer’s working-class spirit remains inseparable from the city that shaped him.
articles.content:
Every year, visitors from around the world make the pilgrimage to the Philadelphia Museum of Art , where 72 stone steps have become one of cinema’s most recognizable landmarks. Many come not for artwork, but to recreate Rocky Balboa’s triumphant ascent, arms raised above the city that made him a legend.

But when Sylvester Stallone first raced up those steps in 1976, Philadelphia was a far cry from the tourist destination immortalized on screen.

At the time, the city was struggling economically, with its aging neighborhoods and industrial character reflecting the hardships faced by many of its residents. Rather than shy away from those realities, the filmmakers embraced them. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies The Underdog Story Behind the Underdog Story Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat'

“We very much wanted to show the city as it was from the viewpoint of Rocky, from the viewpoint of a working-class guy,” producer Irwin Winkler said.

From the rowhouses and neighborhood streets of South Philadelphia to the modest pet shop where Adrian worked, Rocky captured a community of ordinary people trying to make ends meet. Rocky collected debts for a loan shark, Adrian struggled with her confidence, and Paulie was rough around the edges, but beneath their imperfections were characters whose humanity made them relatable, Winkler recalled.

One of the film's most enduring images wasn't even part of the original screenplay, according to I Play Rocky director Peter Farrelly .

With the production operating on a limited budget, the filmmakers relied heavily on the newly developed Steadicam , invented the year prior by cinematographer Garrett Brown . The Steadicam allowed filmmakers to follow moving subjects with unprecedented freedom, and Rocky director John G. Avildsen recruited Brown to operate his new invention for the now iconic “Rocky Steps” sequence. The result transformed a simple training run into a universal image of triumph, with Rocky reaching the top of the steps and raising his arms toward the Philadelphia skyline. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Five decades later, the steps remain a destination for generations of moviegoers, while Rocky Balboa has become one of Philadelphia’s most enduring cultural ambassadors—a fictional underdog whose determination and resilience have come to embody the city’s working-class spirit.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Super's Manga Deserves to Return From Hiatus to End Its Story
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha Dragon Ball Super has been on an indefinite hiatus for the past two years, and the manga deserves to get a proper grand finale with a return for at least one more arc so fans can say goodbye. Dragon Ball Super is in such a strange place right now when it comes to the franchise […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Dragon Ball Super has been on an indefinite hiatus for the past two years, and the manga deserves to get a proper grand finale with a return for at least one more arc so fans can say goodbye. Dragon Ball Super is in such a strange place right now when it comes to the franchise on a whole. A new remake anime series is airing new episodes this Fall as it adapts the classic TV anime from the very beginning , and a brand new anime is in the works for the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc.

But even as the anime is back in action with these new projects, they also aren't technically that "new" in the grand scheme of things. Following the passing of legendary creator Akira Toriyama in 2024, each of the "new" projects for the franchise has been working within the past timeline of the Dragon Ball series. All the while, Dragon Ball Super' s manga has been on hold with no signs of moving the story forward anytime soon. It just needs to return to resolve its final cliffhanger, at least.

Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol has been announced as a brand new anime adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc from the Toyotaro illustrated manga series. Unlike the other arcs seen in the series, this arc was entirely new and had not been adapted or inspired by what was seen in the anime. This new arc introduced a powerful new villain, new transformations, and more with the tease of an expanded universe from that point on. Which then continued with another arc, Granolah the Survivor.

These arcs were then followed by the manga's adaptation of the Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero film, and that's where the manga left off when it went on hiatus back in 2024 . While it had seemed like a suitable ending at the time due to both Toriyama's passing and the fact that it was also now set at the final story in the Dragon Ball Super timeline, the anime has thrown a wrench into things that only exacerbate one of the lingering cliffhangers that manga fans have yet to see fully resolved. And the anime is going to reach this cliffhanger sooner than not.

The Granolah the Survivor Arc ends with the reveal that Frieza had become the new strongest warrior in the universe after training in a Hyperbolic Time Chamber he stumbled on in space, and this had been the explanation as to why Goku and Vegeta had been seen training together with Broly on Beerus' planet during Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . With the anime likely eventually adapting this arc after the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc, its also going to hit the wall of that cliffhanger too. It's just going to be even tougher of a cliffhanger, however, as by that point it will be the final anime story that fans will see.

The only way to avoid this eventual fate is for Dragon Ball Super 's manga to return for at least one final arc to resolve the Black Frieza cliffhanger. It would also serve as a perfect way to say goodbye as one last final fight with arguably Dragon Ball 's most iconic villain would also be a great way to bookend how far Dragon Ball Super had evolved from its original incarnation. A godly battle against Frieza (and potentially even more ) with Ultra Instinct Goku and Ultra Ego Vegeta at full mastery will also be a big enough fight to feel like it's fitting of the franchise's current scale.

Dragon Ball Super basically opened a can of worms when it introduced gods and a multiverse when it first began, and unfortunately will never really be able to tap into the full potential of such an idea even after everything that has happened. Given that the franchise has been under such a tight lock and key since Toriyama's passing, all fans could probably hope for is at least one final story to help end the series for good. Artist Toyotaro has never been shy about his wanting to return to the series , so it's time to make good on that promise.

If the manga never does return to settle the Black Frieza story, there's a potential the anime moves forward with it instead in the coming years. That's entirely possible given that now the anime team can technically make brand new materials for the series with releases like Dragon Ball Daima seen before , but that was also the final project supervised by Toriyama. It's been a complicated web of licenses and rights over the last couple of years, but fans just want a sign that the story will get a proper end.

Do you want to see Dragon Ball Super 's manga return to end its story? Do you want to see the series go on for much longer? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: From Book Club to Netflix: How Katherine Center’s ‘The Bodyguard’ Became ‘Guarding Stars’
articles.summary: Genevieve and Jared Padalecki found Katherine Center’s novel through a book club. The director, writers and producers detail how the rom-com came together and why they kept its readers in mind at every stage.
articles.content:
Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

When director Liz Allen Rosenbaum first scrolled through BookTok, she had an epiphany. The Purple Hearts director, whose credits also include Aquamarine, the upcoming Aquamarine pilot for Disney and Ramona and Beezus, kept finding fan-made lists of the romance tropes readers love most: enemies to lovers, forced proximity and only one bed. She recognized some from her own work. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business New York Knicks Star Josh Hart Inks Two-Book Deal With HarperCollins (Exclusive) Movies Lee Chang-dong on the Mysteries and Meaning of 'Possible Love'

“Oh my God, I’ve been called out. I’m a cliché,” she remembers thinking. Then she started taking notes.

By the time she was developing the Netflix romance film Guarding Stars , those notes had become a working checklist. “Any time there wasn’t enough enemies-to-lovers in the script, I’d say, ‘We need more enemy here! Where’s the enemy?’” Rosenbaum tells The Hollywood Reporter .

Those notes and being attuned to what fans of the book and romance readers want ended up shaping her new film Guarding Stars , Netflix's adaptation of Katherine Center's 2022 novel The Bodyguard , which premieres Nov. 18. Leighton Meester stars as Hannah Brooks, a bodyguard assigned to protect movie star Jack Stapleton ( Jared Padalecki ) who ends up posing as his girlfriend while staying with him at his family's Montana ranch over the holidays. But just as readers were top of mind for Rosenbaum, the film's road to the screen started with that audience too. Producer Genevieve Padalecki selected Center‘s book for her Instagram book club, which led to an Instagram Live with the author and, months later, an option. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As studios and streamers turn to romance novels for their built-in audiences, the people who made Guarding Stars say they kept Center's fans in mind at every step, from the script to the Easter eggs to the test screenings. In separate conversations with THR , members of the creative team behind the film detail how the new holiday romance came together.

Author Katherine Center and Genevieve Padelecki first bonded after Padelecki selected The Bodyguard as her online book club pick. The kinship led to interest in adapting it.

KATHERINE CENTER (AUTHOR): Gen got in touch and said she wanted to feature The Bodyguard in her online book club. Back then it was just Instagram. Of course I said yes, and we did an Instagram Live together, and I instantly fell madly in love with Genevieve Padalecki, because she's a book person. She had the best possible book-person, English-major energy. When you're a writer and you talk to a lot of readers, you can tell when somebody genuinely loves books for all the right reasons, people who just love getting lost in stories. The minute I met her, I thought, "Oh, she loves stories." I could have gone for 10 hours.

I thought that would be that. What a lovely treat. Then, maybe six months later they circled back about wanting to option it. I said, yes, please, no pressure. And I don't know how we got here, but here we are.

GENEVIEVE PADALECKI (PRODUCER): One thing I love about Katherine's books is that they have strong female leads who aren't wilting flowers. They're women with a struggle, a backstory. They're not crippled by the chips in their armor; it actually reinforces them. And then on top of that, you have the flip side of the bodyguard story: a tiny, petite, Lilliputian female bodyguard guarding a male celebrity. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I immediately thought, this would be so fun for Jared [Padalecki]. The book has all the wonderful tropes we love in a rom-com, the things we come back to and watch on repeat. So I turned to Jared and said, "We have to find a way to partner with Katherine and bring this to life."

After finding a home at Netflix, a team was assembled including director Liz Allen Rosenbaum and producers and co-writers Gina Matthews, Grant Scharbo, Erin Cardillo and Richard Keith.

PADALECKI: When we came to Netflix with this story, they got it immediately. They loved this story so much, and it just became a natural fit.

GINA MATTHEWS (PRODUCER/CO-WRITER): Netflix reached out to us [herself and producer-husband Grant Scharbo] when they were considering the book. Jared and Gen had brought it to them, and they were looking for people who had produced and written a lot in the rom-com and holiday space, because Gen and Jared were new to that as producers. I produced What Women Want , 13 Going on 30 and Isn't It Romantic . It's a genre that's really close to our hearts, and it's hard to do well.

We loved Katherine's book because of the way she writes characters, and she's not afraid to go to emotional places. It's funny, and it's high-concept; it has everything that makes a book a solid, strong movie adaptation. But what we also loved is that there's real heart and real trauma these characters have to get over on this journey, inside a big, fun holiday romantic comedy with action. We love movies that take audiences on that ride, where you're laughing, and then you're crying, and you're like, "Oh my God, I was literally laughing 20 minutes ago, and now I'm in tears." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

RICHARD KEITH (PRODUCER/CO-WRITER): Gina sent it to us [himself and producer/co-writer] Erin Cardillo] to see if we were interested. I put the audiobook on [while] leaving L.A., and about two hours in, I had to pull over to charge the car. I texted Gina: "Oh my God, we have to do this movie. I'm obsessed with this book!“ Erin and I are both huge fans of old-school, Richard Curtis-style rom-coms, and there are very few where the two leads get to spend most of the movie together.

ERIN CARDILLO (PRODUCER/CO-WRITER): I just loved it! She's a delightful writer: whimsical and funny, with characters so specifically drawn. We both fell in love with it.

LIZ ALLEN ROSENBAUM (DIRECTOR): It came to me as a director-for-hire project, and I'd been really choosy about those, because I was developing my own material. But my agent said, "It's a go movie. You should really take it seriously." So I read it, and the moment Hannah flips Jack on that tarmac, I thought, "Oh! I've actually never seen anything like this" where the woman was the strong one. I've only done female-oriented projects my whole career, and I'd never seen anything where the woman was the strong one. I had to put everything else aside for a minute and make this.

With a built-in audience already for Center's bestseller, the creative team always had readers at top of mind when sorting out how to bring it to life onscreen.

ROSENBAUM: Believe it or not, almost every movie and pilot I've done has been based on a book. But Purple Hearts [which Rosenbaum directed] came as BookTok was taking off, and I wasn't really acquainted with it. It had a very small budget and no big marketing campaign, and when it started to take off, I was like, "What's happening?" We knocked The Gray Man , a $200 million movie, right off the top spot, and it was because of that grassroots groundswell of well-read, cool women. So I started spending all this time on BookTok accounts, trying to understand it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

They kept talking about tropes, and I grew up thinking those were bad. They make lists of the tropes they love [including] “enemies to lovers,“ “there's only one bed“ and you've got to have “forced proximity.“ These are all words I've learned. The first time I said one, I'd have died of embarrassment: "Oh my God, I've been called out. I'm a cliché." But then I started taking notes. And I realized tropes are good, and I love tropes!

So on Guarding Stars , any time there wasn't enough enemies-to-lovers in the script, I'd say, "We need more enemy here! Where's the enemy?" We did a few drafts after I came on board, and there are plenty of things in this movie that I learned from what people enjoy and want. I'm feeding off the audience too, and I love them.

MATTHEWS: We love that enemies-to-lovers trope. We really do. That conflict, getting under each other's skin, is one of our most fun things to write.

GRANT SCHARBO (PRODUCER/CO-WRITER): Having a built-in audience definitely does not make it easier. You have this fear of disappointment.

MATTHEWS: For Gen, with her book club, she really knows the emotional core of what's going to resonate with those fans. And ironically, those fans are movie fans. Book fans and movie fans are the same in this genre.

PADALECKI: Katherine's fans in the book world are akin to the Supernatural fans. She has a very loud, excited audience. What was so fun was making sure we reached out to that audience. We did a thing about the title, and we made sure there were Easter eggs throughout that are very important to the story. Katherine's input in keeping us on track was integral to making this film. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

MATTHEWS: Everybody shared the same North Star: What are the most important things in the book that Katherine's readers care about? The parts you found so emotional you cried? Or the part where she flips him at the opening of the movie, which is in the trailer? We wanted to keep those touchstones, especially because we weren't able to use the title The Bodyguard . Of course we all wanted to, but there's only one Bodyguard movie!

ROSENBAUM: Katherine knows her audience so well. I don't just mean psychologically. I mean she actually knows them. She makes a point of it and does so many things in person. Jared and Genevieve do that too. It's this cyclical, beautiful circle that keeps feeding itself. And Katherine guided me through that. She knows what readers love about her book, and it's been really helpful to have her blessing and her guidance.

Casting Jared Padalecki, "a rat-a-tat-tat, Bogart-and-Bacall romantic lead, “ and Leighton Meester, the "rom-com heroine we've all been waiting for" as the film's leads.

PADALECKI: I said, "Jared, you have to read this book. It's so fun." At the time he was filming Walker ; we were juggling three kids, and we were just coming out of the pandemic. He read it and was so excited. I don't want to speak for him, but I think initially he was a little nervous. He'd never played a very confident, swaggering character like Jack Stapleton. But he was a pretty easy sell. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

ROSENBAUM: Jared was already attached when I came on board. It felt like a perfect fit. Before I signed on the dotted line, I watched a lot of his material. What hooked me was all his behind-the-scenes footage, because his character on Supernatural wasn't a flirty, bantery character. But there's an enormous amount of BTS on the internet with his co-star, and they're so funny together. He's a born rat-a-tat-tat, Bogart-and-Bacall romantic lead. I mean, part of the reason he hadn't done a movie in a long time is because he'd been so busy and sought after for 20-some-odd years. I mean, who has that streak? He happened to be available. I was like, this is just perfect.

CENTER: Jared Padalecki was born to play Jack! He totally nailed everything about that character. And can I also say he should just be in every rom-com ever?

KEITH: He was instrumental in the development of the script. He and Gen loved the book, and he was adamant that we stay true to who Jack was. But in the book, Jack is pretty wonderful. His flaws are few and far between. To Jared's credit, and some actors shy away from this, he really wanted to find some flaws in this man so we could give him room to grow. It was awesome to see him do that, especially in the scenes with Noah LaLonde. They're really moving. The love story between the two brothers is just as integral to the plot as the love story between Leighton and Jared's characters.

MATTHEWS: Jared had a lot to do, because Jack is kind of a jerk. It's the same as Mel Gibson in What Women Want . He could get away with so much because he was so charming. You're like, "I want to smack you, but I kind of want to kiss you!“ blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

ROSENBAUM: Leighton's a queen. She doesn't have to audition anymore. I'd worked with her on Gossip Girl , just one episode, way back when it was getting started, but you learn enough in a few weeks to see the depth of somebody. She was so sharp with her comedy as Blair Waldorf. And apparently she had made a wish, or a New Year's resolution, that action comedy would come her way, and then we sent her the script.

CARDILLO: When her name came up in the casting process, we were both like, "Oh my God, yes, that would be so great." She's unsuspecting as a bodyguard. You don't think of her that way, but she really is tough in this movie, and it's something we haven't seen her do before.

KEITH: It needs to be someone unassuming enough to be Jared's bodyguard without the parents suspecting but with that innate strength. I'd like to think we wrote a lot of funny lines for her, but she was never playing at being a bodyguard. She never acted like she was aware of the jokes.

PADALECKI: I remember in some of our first meetings, her descriptions of how she saw the characters brought so much depth and humor that I didn't even know was in Hannah. She's truly one of the hardest-working humans I've ever met.

CENTER: She's the rom-com heroine we've all been waiting for. She does this perfect balance of tough but vulnerable. You want somebody you can admire, with a lot of moxie. But I also want her to break my heart a little bit. Yes, in real life she's a movie star. But in this movie, she's me. She can take Jared Padalecki and flip him over like that, but there are also things that scare her. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

MATTHEWS: You can write that crackle on the page, but you don't know how it's going to be. Neither of them comes at it from a place that feels false or disingenuous. It was really about character for both of them, and they brought those scenes to life in a way we couldn't have dreamed of.

The team shifted the story to become a holiday film that serves as a "love story to families."

SCHARBO: We made it a Christmas movie. In the book, it was Thanksgiving. It's a beloved book, and we know we have to make changes to adapt it, so it's a lot of pressure to adapt something people love. We ran a lot of things by Katherine. "How do you feel about this?" And she would say, "I think they'll be OK with that."

CENTER: My books are emotionally cozy. I want them to feel like a hug in story form. When you're telling a story in visuals, and you have the contrast between very cold, snowy stuff outside and fireplaces and twinkle lights and candles inside, it helps you tell that story. This is a story about people who are out in the cold at the start, and then they find a way to reconnect with their families and themselves. You don't just understand it intellectually; you feel it.

CARDILLO: The book takes place over a longer period, and for a feature, condensing the time frame made a lot of sense. It makes it a little bigger for a movie, more fun to play with those holiday tropes. The stakes of spending Christmas with your family, versus just a stretch of time with them, were really appealing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

KEITH: In movies, you want those scenes where you go, "Here's where the movie really starts." Andie MacDowell lying in a bed saying, "Well, you guys are going to stay for Christmas, right?" is such a concrete way into the concept that it was a no-brainer.

ROSENBAUM: The story is really a love story to families. [Hannah]'s not only falling in love with [Jack]; she's falling in love with the family, and she never knew she needed that. With movies, you have to turbocharge things. To me, Christmas is everything family is about. It's the one time a year I see my whole extended family. You need a bigger holiday, where everybody's home, people fly in and there's magic. When I came on board, I had a big meeting with Netflix about making it even more about family.

KEITH: We really loved the parents' relationship being aspirational for the two leads. It has obviously informed the sons' opinions of what love should be, but we wanted that for Leighton's character as well. She grew up with a broken picture of what love could or should be. We really loved that in the book she's not just falling in love with this guy, but with this family, and with the understanding that she deserves to be loved. It's a love story on many levels.

PADALECKI: This is Katherine's baby. She worked on this for a long time to put these words, these ideas and these characters onto the page. articles.title: The Underdog Story Behind the Underdog Story
articles.summary: Fifty years after Sylvester Stallone defied Hollywood’s expectations with 'Rocky,' the film’s unlikely rise from independent production to cultural phenomenon continues to inspire fans to go the distance.
articles.content:
When Sylvester Stallone first walked into the offices of producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff , he was another struggling actor looking for his big break. The producers weren’t casting anything at the time, but as Stallone prepared to leave, he mentioned that he was also a writer. Intrigued, they invited him to send over a screenplay.

Although Winkler and Chartoff passed on the initial script, they recognized Stallone’s potential and encouraged him to share whatever he wrote next.

A week later, he returned with Rocky . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat' Movies Golden Globes: 'I Play Rocky' Submitted as Comedy (Exclusive)

“We thought it was really a great script,” Winkler recalled, nearly 50 years after the film’s release. "It was a story about somebody who has very little and believes in himself.”

There was just one catch: Stallone insisted on playing the title character himself.

“The studios were against it,” Winkler said. "They didn’t want to do the movie in general, and they certainly didn’t want to do it with him. But we persevered, just like he does in the movie.”

Inspired in part by the real-life heavyweight bout between Muhammad Ali and underdog Chuck Wepner, the film’s central message was simple: Winning wasn’t necessarily about defeating your opponent, but proving you belonged in the ring in the first place.

Working with an approximately $1 million budget, Winkler and Chartoff personally guaranteed the production’s costs, ultimately covering roughly $25,000 in overages themselves. The limited budget also forced the filmmakers to get creative.

Take Rocky and Adrian’s romantic outing at the ice-skating rink. Initially intended to be a scene surrounded by other skaters, the filmmakers reimagined the scene with Rocky persuading a rink employee to let the couple skate alone after hours. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Because we couldn't afford to hire extras, we did it with nobody, just because of the budget," Winkler said. "I think it's memorable because it's just the two of them alone."

The result was a quietly intimate moment that captured the film’s emotional authenticity. Rather than disguising its modest resources, Rocky embraced them, grounding its characters in the everyday struggles of working-class Philadelphia .

That authenticity would become one of the film’s defining qualities, helping transform a small independent production into an unlikely Hollywood sensation.

For Winkler, the gamble began paying off when Stallone’s performance and composer Bill Conti ’s triumphant score finally came together.

“We saw the strength of his performance, and then Bill Conti’s music on top of it,” Winkler said. “We said, ‘Okay, this is gonna be something.’”

Released in 1976, Rocky became a box-office phenomenon, won three Academy Awards , including Best Picture, and launched a franchise that has endured for half a century.

For filmmaker Peter Farrelly , the impact was immediate.

“I just remember being blown away,” recalled Farrelly, who said he was about 18 years old the first time he saw Rocky in theaters. “I remember coming out of the theater and being like, ‘Woo!’ And I didn’t know what I was wooing about. I was inspired, but to do what, I didn’t know.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Farrelly likened the experience to watching his favorite team win a championship. He immediately began encouraging his friends to see the film, unaware that nearly five decades later, he would direct a movie about Rocky ’s creation.

“Stallone’s story and Rocky’s story are identical, almost,” Farrelly said.

That parallel became the foundation of I Play Rocky , Farrelly’s new film chronicling Stallone’s fight to bring his screenplay to the screen.

For screenwriter Peter Gamble , the project was deeply personal.

After spending years ghostwriting and contributing creatively to successful productions outside of the spotlight, Gamble began searching for an opportunity to establish himself as a writer in his own right.

“I had this really weird experience of having done things that were really big, and people loved it, but they didn’t know me,” Gamble said. “I was invisible. I felt unseen.”

When his manager suggested exploring Stallone’s story as a potential biopic, Gamble immediately recognized something of himself in the struggling actor who refused to accept Hollywood’s limitations.

Inspired by Stallone’s famously rapid writing process, Gamble challenged himself to complete his own screenplay in approximately two weeks. But much like the original Rocky , getting the film made proved considerably more difficult than writing it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The project spent years in development as its producers struggled to secure financing, with the delays ultimately bringing the film’s release into alignment with Rocky ’s 50th anniversary.

For Gamble, the connection between the two films extends beyond their unlikely journeys to the screen. At their core, both are stories about the universal desire to be recognized for what you have to offer.

“Everyone has a moment where you go, ‘I feel like I got something in my heart and my soul that I can offer the universe if only someone would see it,’” Gamble said.

Fifty years later, Rocky remains a reminder that sometimes going the distance is a victory in itself.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Jason Voorhees has hacked and slashed his way out of Hollywood limbo, as the Friday the 13th franchise moves forward on both the big and small screens. The prequel series Crystal Lake became a major breakout hit on Peacock earlier this Fall, while a reboot film was finally put into production. Now, we are getting a slew of details about the reboot, and it sounds like a pretty good setup.

The reboot film will be titled Jason . It will be the 13th film in the franchise, and it has an official release date of Friday, August 13th, 2027. In addition to the title and release date, we also got the first details about the cast of the film.

According to rep orts, Schuyler White (Haunt) will star as Jason Voorhees in Jason ; a stunt coordinator and special effects artist, White played Jason in last year's online short Sweet Revenge , in celebration of Friday the 13th 's 45th anniversary.

“We spent months thinking about how to create the scariest, most imposing Jason and who truly deserved to wear the mask," Friday the 13th "franchise steward" Robbie Barsamian said in a statement. "Beyond his towering physical presence, we knew Schuyler understood what makes Jason tick—and that he had the work ethic and genuine respect for this franchise to get it right."

"He approached this theatrical feature like the role of a lifetime, packing 30 pounds of solid muscle onto his 6’5″ frame and studying the iconic Jasons who came before him so that he feels like an unstoppable force of nature," Barsamian continued. "On set, we framed him low and tight, so the audience is right there in his space, looking up at him. This will be the most intimidating Jason that has ever been on screen.”

Natalie Alyn Lind (Dutton Ranch) will play the film's final girl, Lauren. “Natalie is not only an excellent actress and incredibly hardworking, but also one of the biggest horror enthusiasts and fans of this franchise," Barsamian said. "When you put all that together, you get something special. This franchise has had many strong female leads, but her performance might just be the strongest this franchise has ever had.”

The rest of the cast will include "Matt Cornett ( Every Year After ) as Asher, Lilia Buckingham ( Hocus Pocus 2 ) as Madison, John Owen Lowe ( Unstable ) as Jake, Summer Madison ( The Summer I Turned Pretty ) as Emily, Selena Turner ( Will Trent ) as Olive, Matthew Keoni Sato ( High School Musical: The Musical: The Series ) as Lucas, Brook Sill ( Stranger Things ) as Zoe, Guillermo Diaz ( Scandal ) as Rick, Johnell Young ( Wu-Tang: An American Saga ) as Frank, Sencere M. Brown ( Homage ) as Chase and Bryan Gael Guzman ( Nickel Boys ) as Dylan."

Steve Miner, who directed Friday the 13th Part 2 (1981) and Friday the 13th Part III (1982), will be returning to direct Jason . Miner is responsible for introducing a lot of the main Jason Voorhees lore, including the hockey mask and machete. David Fliegel is writing the script.

Jason will be released in theaters on August 13, 2027.

articles.title: Up-and-Coming Filmmakers Talk About Their Craft, Challenges, Inspirations and More at Adobe TV & Film Fund Screening
articles.summary: Pursuing a career as a filmmaker isn't for the faint of heart. This week, three young creators who have been supported by the Adobe TV & Film Fund — Leo Aguirre, Michael Lei and Mel Mah — presented their short films at a special screening in Miami Beach hosted by Adobe and spoke about their […]
articles.content:
Pursuing a career as a filmmaker isn't for the faint of heart. This week, three young creators who have been supported by the Adobe TV & Film Fund — Leo Aguirre, Michael Lei and Mel Mah — presented their short films at a special screening in Miami Beach hosted by Adobe and spoke about their work and what's next.

Variety moderated the conversation with the filmmakers in partnership with Adobe. The screening took place Nov. 10 at the Fillmore Miami Beach historic Art Deco theater, held during this year's Adobe MAX 2026 creativity conference. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Skydance Sets Comms and Publicity Leadership Team, With Several Execs Departing John Oliver Dunks on Midterms Losers Elon Musk and Haley Stevens

Aguirre, a writer, director and visual artist raised on the U.S.-Mexico border, said his main advice to aspiring filmmakers is to "really believe in yourself."

"No one's going to want to make your movie more than you," he said. "Tell people to get on the train or get out of the way. And I think that's the approach you have to have for your movie."

Mah, a writer, director, and producer from Toronto, said it's important for filmmakers to "remember that art is created from the heart. Your mind is there to help, but it's an emotional medium. And movies, the best ones, no matter what, they're meant to move people." She added that in addition to doing work on your scripts every day, you should "do things outside of film" to explore other passions and hobbies. "That's what actually makes you a great filmmaker, because we're telling stories about real life and you've got to go out there and live it in order to be to be able to tell those stories," Mah said.

Lei, an award-winning Chinese-born filmmaker, emphasized that it's a difficult line of work. "It's a really hard thing that to try to do film and it's probably the most expensive art form, or one of the most expensive art forms, just because the amount of resources it takes to bring a crew and cast together and to do it convincingly," he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"You have to really, really love it and you have to want it for the right reasons," Lei said. "It's not a medium to get wealthy in. It's not a medium to get famous."

Lei's short that screened at the Adobe event was "The Rift," a sci-fi-inflected story about a young man suspected of a mysterious affliction that makes him perceive the world in daylight while everyone, including his own father, sees darkness. Lei said it was the first public screening of "The Rift" — and he said it was gratifying to hear the response of a live audience. "I don't know how to say this in other words, but it's like, I will carry this on a hard day, you know? Like, I will remember this moment a few months from now where the writing is not coming or I get a rejection, but I'll remember this moment and go, 'You know, that's what it's worth it. This is what it's for, exactly.'"

Lei said "The Rift" will hopefully be a gateway for the story to become a feature-length film. "It's a script that I've been carrying for the better part of the 2020s. And to have the opportunity through Adobe to actually go and film this proof of concept taught us so much," he said.

Aguirre's short film "Isme" is about a tempestuous NYC teenager who steals a necklace from a woman on her deathbed — and "develops an obsession that leads her down a spiritually perilous path," per the logline. "It's a film about what we hold in this life and then what we hold in the next," Aguirre said. "We all grew up with this idea of who we need to be. And then there's artifice. And sometimes we feel completed by something that's material."

Aguirre's script for his debut feature, "Verano," was selected for the 2025 Sundance Screenwriters & Directors Lab and is a recipient of the 2025-2026 Academy Nicholl Fellowship. "Verano," which was supported by Adobe, was shot over the summer and Aguirre is hoping to premiere the film in the spring of 2027.

"It was hard to get money. It was hard to get people to commit to helping us out," said Aguirre. "But it was it was a very beautiful experience in so many ways." Making "Isme" helped prepare him to embark on the feature film because he learned "how can we scale down and try to make the most of what we have."

Mah, who is a 2024 Women in Film directing fellow and founder of Decorum Pictures, also saw her short film "And That’s The Way The Cookie Crumbles" debut at the Adobe screening. The synopsis: A yoga influencer spirals into an existential crisis when a fortune cookie predicts her imminent death, and she begins to expose the hypocrisy of the mindfulness empire she’s built around a life she doesn’t actually live. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"There's so many things up there that I would have done differently, but there are so many things that also fell into place beautifully, too," Mah said about her short film. "And I think that's part of the beauty of filmmaking is we actually don't have as much control as we think." The story was somewhat autobiographical (Mah is herself a yoga and mindfulness teacher), but she said actress Dia Frampton, who plays the main character, "surprised me by bringing so much more of her spin on it. And I think because I'm so close to the character, I had imagined it maybe more in the way that I would be in that situation. But pleasantly surprised at how the performance was different."

Mah is currently developing her debut feature film "This Way to Home," a road-trip dramedy starring Ken Jeong, with filming scheduled for spring 2027. "This Way to Home" was selected for Gold House’s Gold Pitch program at the Toronto International Film Festival and has secured CAN$1 million in production financing from Telefilm Canada.

Each of the filmmakers were encouraged by the boom at the theatrical box office in 2026 , the best year for the industry since COVID. "I am a hopeless optimist, and I really think that we're always going to be going to the theaters," Mah said. "I don't think anything's going to replace that. And I do think there's something in us that craves being in a room, quiet, seated all together and getting to experience the same emotions."

The trio also recounted how they realized they wanted to become filmmakers.

Said Mah, "I've always been a storyteller, but maybe in a different way. My first passion was dance. I was a professional dancer for a long time, and that's what took me from Toronto to Los Angeles originally. So from a young age, I started learning how to tell stories non-verbally and with my body. And then it was actually once I was living in Los Angeles that I started making my own dance films. And that's when I realized that I wanted to step into filmmaking." She added that her father "raised me on really great films. He taught me how to edit with Adobe."

Five years later, the project has gained new momentum, as Erik Jendresen ( Band of Brothers ) and Howard A. Rodman ( Savage Grace ) have come aboard to pen the period thriller for Hacksaw Ridge producer David Permut 's Permut Presentations and AETH Entertainment .

Set at the height of the Cold War, Goldsboro tells the extraordinary true story of the January 1961 crash of a U.S. Air Force B-52 near Goldsboro, North Carolina. The aircraft was carrying two thermonuclear weapons when it broke apart in midair, sending the bombs toward the farmland below and bringing the United States to the brink of nuclear catastrophe. The film will explore the experiences of the Goldsboro townsfolk, the military personnel confronting the crisis, and the human decisions made in the shadow of a catastrophe that could have changed the course of history. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News How Indie Comedy 'The Invite' Crashed The Summer Blockbuster Party; Is The Next Stop Broadway? Dobson, a former U.S. Air Force officer who served with Strategic Air Command during the 1960s, spent years researching the Goldsboro incident and interviewing many of the people directly involved. His book provides a detailed account of the doomed B-52 mission, its crew, the recovery operation, and the circumstances and war games surrounding one of the most extraordinary nuclear incidents of the Cold War. The story's themes carry new weight today, with the advent of AI, a technology Bill Gates has warned "makes nuclear weapons look like nothing," posing the threat of great disruption.

Coming off a pair of lauded 2026 releases — the A24 chamber drama The Invite and Apple disability rights drama Being Heumann — Permut told Deadline, "Some true stories almost defy belief, and GOLDSBORO is one of them." He's set to produce alongside Eric Woods and Carla Woods for AETH Entertainment, Michael Alfieri and Sterling Macer, Jr.

Permut Presentations' Head of Development, Alex Astrachan, will serve as executive producer. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Eric Woods of AETH said, "We knew the key to telling this story would be finding the humanity within an event of such enormous historical significance. Erik Jendresen and Howard Rodman are extraordinary storytellers with a remarkable ability to bring complex, character-driven stories to life. They are the ideal team to explore the lives of the people caught in the middle of this extraordinary event."

No stranger to war stories, Jendresen served as lead writer and supervising producer of HBO's acclaimed WWII miniseries Band of Brothers , sharing in its Emmy win for Outstanding Miniseries and receiving an Emmy nomination for writing. His recent feature work includes co-writing Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning and Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning with Christopher McQuarrie.

Rodman is a screenwriter, novelist and educator whose credits include Savage Grace , starring Julianne Moore and Eddie Redmayne; August ; and Joe Gould’s Secret . His screenplay for Savage Grace received an Independent Spirit Award nomination. A former chair of USC's screenwriting program and an Artistic Director of the Sundance Screenwriting Labs, he's a past President of the Writers Guild of America West and is currently Vice President of AMPAS.

Permut's The Invite grossed over $62M worldwide — no small feat for an indie drama in the 2020s — and was just nominated for four Gotham Awards, including Best Picture. AETH Entertainment's Eric and Carla Woods have produced over 150 films and series, with credits including Looking Through Water starring Michael Douglas, Christmas with the Campbells , Spread , and Incarcerated .

David Ellison covered a lot of ground and jumped over some landmines today at the New York Times Dealbook summit, but things got positively testy when it came to the topic of a federal tax credit for film and television.

"When you look at who this incentive helps, the misnomer out there is you're giving Tom Cruise a tax break," the Skydance CEO told the power crowd packed into Lincoln Center on Wedbesday. "That's not true."

Pushing back on host Andrew Ross Sorkin 's claim that lucrative tax credits do little to produce "measurable gains in jobs, wages, and economic growth," Ellison insisted that a lot of his much battered relationship with Donald Trump and MAGA has been about getting a national plan in place as it has been about seeing his acquisition of Paramount and his $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery closed. The second season wrapped up in March last year, and since then, fans have been anticipating the release window and even a trailer for the movie. While the light novel and webtoon have long since reached their conclusions, the anime still has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The second season wrapped up the Jeju Island Arc , where Jinwoo revealed his true powers in front of the entire world. Things will only continue to get more intense from here on out, and no doubt, Jinwoo will continue to level up even now.

However, along with Jinwoo, his shadows will also continue to become more powerful as they encounter powerful opponents along the way. As of now, Jinwoo has an incredible lineup of powerful shadows that were extracted from the opponents he has defeated so far. His most powerful shadow in the anime so far is Beru, who was previously the Ant King from the S-Rank dungeon on Jeju Island. The official X handle of the anime drops stunning visuals of Jinwoo's shadows, namely Igris, Beru, Kaisel, Tank, Iron, and Kiba.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Lilo & Stitch is coming to theaters with an animated revival bringing back the classic franchise for a new generation, and a new sneak peek is showing off the first look at its new short in motion. With Disney's next major outing, Hexed , hitting theaters over the Thanksgiving holiday teasing it's going to be the end of one era of Walt Disney Animation Studios , it's incredibly fitting that screenings of the film are going to be offering a first look at what could end up being the start of the next era for the studio.

Lilo & Scratch is a brand new animated short that will be screening ahead of Hexed , and features the original Lilo & Stitch animated incarnations coming back in a whole new kind of way. The most impressive aspect of the new short is the fact that while it looks like the 2D animated original feature film, it's actually been animated through the CG animation pipeline at the studio to make a cool new kind of end result. You can check it out in motion below with a special sneak peek clip.

View this post on Instagram Lilo & Scratch will be debuting across theaters on November 25th together with screenings of Disney's Hexed , so you're going to want to make it to the theater a bit early to make sure to catch the new short in action. Directed by Malcon Pierce and Fawn Veerasunthorn, it's the first new animated short from Walt Disney Animation Studios in five years. Using the already set CG animation pipeline with the studio, the new short adapts it to the original 2D animation designs that helps to make it a whole new kind of fluid for a new generation of fans.

Maia Kealoha returns from the live-action Lilo & Stitch and its now in the works sequel as Lilo while Chris Sanders reprises his role as Stitch. As the sneak peek teases, Lilo adopts a mysterious cat that is clearly hiding a rambunctiousness that Stitch is likely going to be contending with in secret. It's not clear how long this new short will last, but it's certainly an exciting release given that it lays out a potential future for more of this 2D-like animated releases coming from Disney in the future. Which would be a big deal to the older fans.

Lilo & Stitch' s live-action feature film reboot had been an incredible success for Disney at the box office, and quickly went into development on its sequel. Lilo & Stitch 2 is currently in the works for a release in Summer 2028 , but a concrete release date has yet to be revealed as of this time. Very little has been revealed for the new sequel, but it's been confirmed that it will be introducing a new take on Angel, who was one of the many Experiments that had been unleashed in the TV animated series.

Lilo & Stitch 's live-action reboot had sparked some debates among fans for some of the changes it had made with its ending, and that's likely going to continue with the sequel as the stars behind it have teased that it's also going to make changes from the original version . But with a direct to video sequel and a full TV series to draw inspiration from, it's likely going to be packed with surprises. How are you liking the look of Lilo & Scratch so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Celebrity Beauty Brands (Even Kim’s) Are Failing. Here Are the New Rules
articles.summary: Jennifer Aniston, Kate Hudson, Cardi B and top branding consultants weigh in on what separates the infamous flops from the billion-dollar breakouts.
articles.content:
G wen Stefani's GXVE Beauty is gone. So are Scarlett Johansson 's skin care line The Outset and Serena Williams' Wyn Beauty cosmetics. Even Kim Kardashian 's KKW Beauty and SKKN by Kim have been retired. Blake Lively 's Blake Brown Beauty hair care is struggling, and Jennifer Lopez 's JLO Beauty has quietly exited Sephora. Yes, the celebrity beauty business is crowded and unforgiving, but that still hasn't stopped Cardi B and Jennifer Lawrence from joining the fray.

Cardi B, for one, remains undeterred. "People are always going to have something to say, but I didn't create Grow-Good just to put my name on a bottle. Hair care has always been personal to me. I've been sharing my hair routines, my homemade treatments and my hair journey with my fans for years, way before I ever thought about launching a brand." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories THR Digital Cover Hudson Williams and His Hairstylist Aika Flores Really Are That Close THR Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty's Next Billion-Dollar Mogul

With a stake in a brand worth potentially far more than a movie deal as production slates threaten to continue shrinking, it's easy to understand why Hollywood keeps lining up. The success stories are seductive: Rihanna 's Fenty Beauty helped make her a billionaire, Selena Gomez 's Rare Beauty has been valued at $2.7 billion, and Hailey Bieber's Rhode sold to e.l.f. Beauty in a deal worth up to $1 billion.

But fame doesn't always bring fortune — or an easy ride. In October, Lawrence launched Mes (pronounced "mess") with Arcaea CEO Jasmina Aganovic, generating plenty of buzz and a fair amount of backlash over what online critics complained was another example of celebrity overreach. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The partnership reportedly began after Lawrence watched Aganovic deliver a TED Talk about the future of cosmetics. Aganovic leads Arcaea, a biotech company developing sustainable, high-performance cosmetic ingredients that has counted Chanel among its investors, and she brings serious beauty credentials, having previously worked at Living Proof and led skin-microbiome brand Mother Dirt. Mes embraces an "unbothered beauty" philosophy, with the enticing promise of achieving great hair without putting in lots of time or effort. It also plays into Lawrence's public persona as the rare A-lister with genuinely self-deprecating, what-you-see-is-what-you-get candor. The actress introduced the line, which includes a hair mask, serum and volume mist, on Instagram as one for "nice people who don't leave mean comments." It was almost as if she knew what was coming. (Per her reps, Lawrence was not available to comment for this report.)

After years away from social media, Lawrence made her debut Sept. 9, just weeks before the launch, and the timing didn't go unnoticed. Some commenters smelled a calculated sales pitch. Others questioned the fit, noting she's never been especially known for her hair. To skeptics and Reddit users, it looked like one more celebrity chasing a Rhode-sized payday. Lawrence, for her part, said the line grew out of years in the glam chair, when she would wash her hair only once a week.

"At this point in the life cycle of celebrity brands, the initial reaction is always going be the eye roll," says Aliza Licht, marketing veteran and author of On Brand . "We all have the playbook now and everybody knows what's behind the curtain." Often, that's a licensing deal, a manufacturer, a hefty marketing budget and a carefully crafted backstory, with the star's name as the cherry on top. "Consumers are good at recognizing an engineered marketing narrative dressed up as a personal passion project." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Beauty publicist Marie-Laure Fournier, founder of Fournier PR + Consulting, believes the criticism around Mes is still manageable. "A candid, even humorous video with Aganovic, whether with a magazine or on social media, could go a long way toward humanizing the launch and addressing the skepticism head on," she says. "The public wants to see that you're listening, learning and willing to adapt."

Despite some of the backlash, the early industry read on Mes is cautiously optimistic. Lawrence's working with Aganovic is "a good move, to partner with a brand like Arcaea that is well established in the beauty industry," says Clare Hennigan, principal analyst for beauty and consumer goods at global research firm Mintel. Hennigan also sees promise in the products, particularly a gel hair mask that can be applied to dry hair and doubles as a styler. No need to wait for wash day. "They are solving a pain point of convenience, a key motivator for purchases," she says. "Anything that makes life a little easier is something shoppers will pay more for."

Kate Hudson would applaud this solution-oriented approach for the consumer. The celebrity entrepreneur co-founded Fabletics in 2013, remains a shareholder and watched the activewear company reportedly surpass $1 billion in revenue in 2025. "You can have the most beautiful vision in the world, but once you put something out there, you have to pay attention to what they need, what they love and what they don't," she says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Delivering effective products is one thing; fostering a genuine connection with the consumer is another. Cardi B out of the gate demonstrated a keen understanding of the latter with marketing Grow-Good. Her grassroots strategy focuses on neighborhood beauty supply stores, including shops in her native Bronx. The hair care line, following three years of development, debuted in April and reportedly sold out in less than 35 minutes. "Listen, I know my people because I am my people!" she says. "I grew up going to beauty supply stores. Those stores have always been part of our community, and I wanted Grow-Good to be there too. For me, it was about making sure the products were accessible to the people I created them for." Lisa Motzko Hamilton, former vp of merchandising at Ulta Beauty and co-founder of Breakthru Beauty consultancy, says brands perform best when the entertainer is "showing up, engaging with their community and sharing a part of themselves beyond their celebrity status." The Business of Fashion reports a promising 40 percent return-customer rate for Grow-Good.

Even more critically, the celebrity and the product need to make sense together. Lady Gaga's Haus Labs cosmetics draw on her reputation for artistry and creative expression, while Selena Gomez built Rare Beauty around supporting mental health for young people, a cause she has publicly owned as a personal issue, with 1 percent of sales going to Rare Impact Fund. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Hennigan cites Jennifer Aniston 's LolaVie as a brand that gets it very right. Aniston's hairstyles have been a cultural fixture for decades, making hair care a natural fit. She spent several years developing the line before launching in 2021 and has since expanded to Ulta and Credo. "LolaVie is very personal to me. My relationship with my hair, the products I've tried over the years and the challenges I've experienced are what inspired the brand in the first place," says Aniston. "I didn't want to simply put my name on something; I wanted to be part of building something that I truly believed in."

The Morning Show star also makes a point of keeping a conversation going with customers. "I love hearing how other people incorporate the products into their routines and about the results they're seeing. We've made changes to product in the past based on consumer feedback," she says. (She's also extended LolaVie into pet shampoo: "My dogs are such a big part of my family, and I wanted to bring the same thoughtfulness and attention to detail that goes into our human hair care." All profits benefit The Clydeo Fund, which supports animal rescue and rehabilitation.)

Author Licht points to Kardashian as someone who has spent years cultivating "a parasocial bond with followers, so a new brand lands with people she already knows, even the haters." Stars who suddenly surface hawking new products are a harder sell. "It's odd when we hear from celebrities out of the blue," she says. "We don't have social relationships with them, they're movie stars." Licht adds that Lawrence, who had no public social media presence until weeks before the launch, "seemed to come out of thin air," she says. "We are missing a bit of evidence there." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Johansson's The Outset offers another cautionary tale. "We didn't have historical commentary from Scarlett around skin care," says Licht. "The consumer needs to find a germ of a connection between the celebrity and the brand." Hennigan sees another issue: "The problem was proof. The efficacy and science may not have been as visible to shoppers."

Lopez faced a different kind of disconnect with potential consumers. A merchandising executive at a beauty retailer, speaking on condition of anonymity, questions JLO Beauty's origin story. "Jennifer hung the age-defying 'JLo Glow' on a family olive oil secret, but doubters online, including a chorus of dermatologists, weren't convinced it was the whole story with JLO Beauty," creating an issue with consumer trust.

Blake Lively's Blake Brown Beauty hair care line launched to considerable fanfare at Target, only to face a more complicated reality as the actress became embroiled in the fallout surrounding It Ends With Us and her legal battle with Justin Baldoni. Lively went quiet on social media, and sales have reportedly dropped sharply. "The war with Justin was likely a huge detriment to sales," says Licht.

Distribution matters, too. Lady Gaga's Haus Labs initially launched exclusively on Amazon, a challenging fit for color cosmetics, where shoppers want to try on shades before buying. Its move to Sephora introduced the brand to a broader beauty audience. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Then comes the most important question of all: Does the world really need another beauty line?

Fenty Beauty answered that question nearly a decade ago with an expansive and inclusive shade range that addressed a glaring gap in the cosmetics market. Rhode found its opening with accessible pricing on ingredients that had become associated with more expensive skin care. "Peptides were drawing a lot of attention, with many brands charging a premium for them, while Bieber offered high-performing peptide products at a more affordable price," notes Hennigan. For Mes, even in light of its messy debut, Hennigan sees an opportunity to shift the conversation toward time-saving efficiency with education: "Help consumers understand how these products fit into their existing hair care routines. Since the hair mask comes with a learning curve, the brand needs to drive the how-to aspect home" with tutorials and partnerships with pro stylists who can demo the products, she advises.

Ultimately, the biggest challenge of the enterprise may be the least glamorous part: remaining involved long after the cameras and launch parties. Hudson, who joined HealthyCell supplements as an investor and creative strategy partner in October, says patience is the X factor. "I've learned that building a business is a long game," she says. "You have to love the process, not just the excitement of launching something." Licht doesn't mince words: "Most of the time celebrities are just not cut out for the daily grind required to build a brand, and that's why a lot of these lines fail." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: Nicolas Cage on His Approach to Playing John Madden in New Biopic: "I'm Not an Impressionist"
articles.summary: Cage stars alongside Christian Bale in David O. Russell's 'Madden.'
articles.content:
John Madden may be one of the most notable figures in sports history, but he was unknown to Nicolas Cage before the actor portrayed him in new movie Madden .

"He was not on my radar. I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn't interested in team sports whatsoever," Cage, a member of the cinema-centric Coppola family, explains.

That didn't stop David O. Russell from casting him in the film , which follows Madden's journey from a Super Bowl-winning coach to creating the Madden NFL video game and becoming a beloved commentator. Intertwined in that story is Raiders owner Al Davis (played by Christian Bale ), who was Madden's best friend on and off the field; Russell originally came to Cage to play Davis, which he rejected. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale Go for Broke in a Cartoonish Biopic From David O. Russell That's Strictly for Football Fanatics Movies John Mulaney Teases His 'Get Smart' Reboot: "My Favorite Type of Person to Play"

When the director came back with the idea that he play Madden instead, "because I'm someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation," Cage says. "It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me."

"That's what acting's about. I'm not an impressionist, I'm not [Madden impersonator] Frank Caliendo," he continues. "I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I'm trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That's also how Cage approached Madden's famous voice, saying, "I listened to his cadence, I located what I thought would be an interpretation within the realms of what was anatomically possible. I'm not going to let AI touch my voice or my appearance. I try to give you something which is an interpretation."

The film — with a starry supporting cast that includes Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney and Shane Gillis — also brings together two actors who famously go deep into their roles, in Cage and Bale. Cage says the two are "very different kinds of actors" who had a "great time riffing off of each other," while Bale notes that "there's no competition in that at all" in how they face-off on screen.

"I've admired Nic for many, many years, going all the way back to Rumble Fish , which is absolutely one of my favorite movies ever," Bale says. "He's not only a fascinating actor but a very interesting man himself. He's lived a hell of a life, just like Al Davis, just like John Madden, just like David O. Russell. There were some real characters involved in creating this film."

This marks the fourth collaboration between Russell and Bale, following The Fighter , American Hustle and Amsterdam . The star said that when he and the director "approach a film, we always think this might just be the last one we ever get to make. That's the right attitude to have with movies, and in the state of movies right now, it might very well be the truth. articles.content:
David Ellison , chairman and CEO of Skydance , confirmed that tech mogul Elon Musk has invested in the company, formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

Musk, the world's richest person, invested about $1 billion in Skydance post-merger, CNBC and Semafor reported last month. Ellison, speaking Wednesday at the New York Times’ 2026 DealBook Summit at Manhattan's Jazz at Lincoln Center, acknowledged that Musk is a part-owner of Skydance but he did not confirm the investment amount. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Nicole Kidman to Receive Honorary Cesar From French Film Academy

The New York Times' Andrew Ross Sorkin asked Ellison about the reports of Musk investing a billion dollars into Skydance, "and I think some people wanted to know whether this is the beginning of something bigger with Starlink long-term, or is a one-off as a given his relationship with your father," Larry Ellison.

Ellison responded, "So look, I have so much admiration and respect for Elon. I mean, I don't know if you saw recently, but but but literally watching you know Starship, it's a marvel…. I mean, he is both the [Nikola] Tesla and [Thomas] Edison… He is the from my perspective he is the greatest entrepreneur of our time, and he doesn't invest in a lot of companies."

Ellison continued, "So to have his vote of confidence and to have him as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege. And if there was any opportunity to be able to collaborate with him in the future… that is the appropriate opportunity in the future, we'd be thrilled to do so. But there's nothing [right now]."

Ellison’s Paramount Skydance closed its $111 billion megamerger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 , with major backing from his father, Larry Ellison. The company, one of the biggest media and entertainment conglomerates in the industry, has around $80 billion in net debt and is expected to lay off thousands of employees as part of achieving $6 billion in annualized savings by 2029.
