articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Bellevue Productions , the literary management and production company led by President John Zaozirny, has announced the hiring of literary manager David Baggelaar , who joins following more than a decade at Benderspink and its successor company, Good Fear. Bringing with him a roster of film and television writers, directors and IP creators, Baggelaar will continue developing his existing clients while working to expand Bellevue's roster across both film and television. Clients joining Baggelaar include Monisha Dadlani ( The Marigold Paradox ), Julian Terry ( Don't Peek ), Michael Feldman & Debbie Jhoon ( A.P. Bio , Not Dead Yet ), Rohit Kumar ( 13 Reasons Why , Wheel of Time ), Min-Woo Park ( Grey's Anatomy ), Brandi Nicole ( Your Honor , Ballard ), Woody Strassner ( FBI ), Amelia Sims ( S.W.A.T. ) and Barnett Brettler ( Black Mad Wheel ). Baggelaar's production experience includes work on New Line's We're the Millers , Horrible Bosses 2 and Vacation , as well as Disney's Mulan , and serving as an associate producer on A24's Under the Silver Lake . He told us, "From my first conversations with the Bellevue team, I felt an immediate connection. Their client-first approach and genuine dedication to the craft of development are exactly what I was looking for, both for myself and for those I represent, and I couldn't be more excited to build the next chapter of my career here." Bellevue's Zaozirny said, "David's deep industry experience, keen eye for talent, and extensive background in production make him an incredibly exciting manager to work alongside and we're lucky to have him at Bellevue. We can't wait to see how he continues to develop the amazing clients he's already working with and what bold new voices he'll be signing now that he's here." Founded in 2015, Bellevue is known for its knack for breaking emerging writers. Clients have placed 72 scripts on the last 11 Black Lists, with No. 1 scripts in 2016, 2020, 2021 and 2025. The company's upcoming production slate includes Paramount's K-Pop: The Debut and Warner Bros.' Shiver , both scheduled for theatrical release in 2027. articles.title: Gabriel Luna on How Arnold Schwarzenegger's Christmas Party Led Him to 'The Terminal List' and 'Dexter: Resurrection'
articles.summary: Luna also discusses spoilers from his 'Terminal List' and 'Dexter' roles, elaborates on 'The Last of Us' final season and shares his renewed hope of playing Robbie Reyes/Ghost Rider again.
articles.content:
[This story contains spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection seasons two, episode three, “Live Free and Die” and The Terminal List season two.]

Gabriel Luna once told The Hollywood Reporter that he wouldn't trade the friendships he made on the underappreciated Terminator: Dark Fate for the brighter fate of a billion-dollar box office haul. Chief among them was his unexpected bond with one Arnold Schwarzenegger .

From cigar-filled boat rides and chess matches to annual Christmas parties and charitable toy drives , their relationship extends well beyond the two other times they've been castmates after playing dueling Terminators. At this stage of his life, Luna even considers Schwarzenegger a father figure, having been raised in Austin, Texas, by his widowed single mother. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Fourth 'Terminal List' Show in the Works at Prime Video TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners

Luna knew he was in rarefied air when he received an invitation to the Schwarzenegger family Christmas party in 2022, the first since the pandemic forced a two-year hiatus. Rather than the usual sprawling guest list, the gathering had been scaled down from 250 people to just 25. There, he rubbed elbows with Schwarzenegger's son-in-law, Chris Pratt .

The Terminal List , Pratt’s action-thriller series, hadn't officially been renewed for a second season at that point, but the star-executive producer still had a role in mind for Luna, who would eventually play James Reece's (Pratt) former SEAL teammate turned CIA operative, Freddy Strain.

“I got to asking him about how The Terminal List was going, and he said, ‘If we're blessed to get a second season, there's a part that's perfect for you,’” Luna tells THR during his lunch break on the Vancouver-based set of The Last of Us season three. “So that job started as a brotherly handshake in King Arnold's court.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The domino effect didn't stop there. While working on The Terminal List together, Luna caught the attention of director Marcos Siega, who had another casting idea up his sleeve. As an in-house director and executive producer on Dexter: Resurrection , Siega knew the second episode of the show's second season would introduce “The Sleep-Eyed Stranger,” a nocturnal serial killer whose real name is Ray Ballard. So he gauged Luna’s interest on the set of Terminal List 's penultimate episode of season two, and he soon agreed to play his first villain away from Schwarzenegger.

“Personally, I'm drawn to heroic characters. I always try to depict characters that my grandmothers would've been proud of,” Luna says. “So, up to this point, I'd only played bad guys for Arnold Schwarzenegger [in Dark Fate and FUBAR ].”

Naturally, as Dexter's (Michael C. Hall) latest problem to solve, “Sleepy” isn't long for this world. But the experience did give Luna an opportunity to provide his Dexter -loving wife, Smaranda Luna, with the photo of all photos.

“There's a great photo of my girl [next to me as I’m Saran-wrapped on Dexter’s kill table]. She’s a big fan of the show, so she had me right where she wanted me,” Luna recalls mid-laugh. “I joked that she could’ve asked for anything in that moment, and I would've been powerless against her.”

Luna, as Tommy Miller, is currently two-thirds of the way through filming The Last of Us ' third and final season. The series continues to move forward without its former leading man, Pedro Pascal, as well as video game franchise co-creator Neil Druckmann, who parted ways with co-creator and showrunner Craig Mazin between seasons . Luna says the spirit of both Pascal and Druckmann remains very much alive on set, with him, Mazin and co-stars Bella Ramsey and Kaitlyn Dever committed to honoring their previous collaborators. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Bella and I are the longest-tenured people on this set, so we’re carrying the DNA of the story, Neil's intentions and his spirit forward. Craig loves the story that Neil has constructed, and he’s been a very stable steward who honors and maintains the source material,” Luna says. “We're doing our absolute best to bring the most explosive, most heart-wrenching culmination. I just want to give the fans of the game and the fans of the show exactly what they deserve, which is, however morally ambiguous, a very explosive ending.”

Below, in a conversation with THR , Luna also discusses spoiler details from his Terminal List and Dexter roles, elaborates on The Last of Us ' final season and shares his renewed hope of playing Robbie Reyes/ Ghost Rider again.

So The Terminal List season two was last year, Dexter: Resurrection kicked off this year and it’s been The Last of Us season three ever since?

Correct. The Terminal List took us to South Africa, Toronto and Morocco. We wrapped in November of ‘25. Then my contribution to Dexter was shot this past spring over a couple months. And now I 'm here in Vancouver shooting season three of The Last of Us .

I’ve been watching Dexter since day one, and I still can’t quite figure out why I root for this serial killer as much as I do. Have you come up with the answer yet?

My wife, Smaranda, has also been a huge fan of the show since its inception. She got me into a few of the seasons. It might be because we're in his head. We spend so much time with him in his head, and we feel close to him. He's behind enemy lines of our own morality and psyche. He's able to step over that line and infiltrate in that way. So he's become much closer to us than we would ordinarily allow someone like that. Of course, Michael C. [Hall] is such an inviting presence. He's a great actor, and I'm sure that has something to do with it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

You’ve never struck me as someone who could be described as “sleepy-eyed.” What was your reaction to the description of The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger on first read?

Personally, I'm drawn to heroic characters. I always try to depict characters that my grandmothers would've been proud of, but there've been a few exceptions to the rule. Of course, I played a Terminator for Arnold in Terminator: Dark Fate , and then I played a villain again for Arnold on Fubar . So, up to this point, I'd only played bad guys for Arnold Schwarzenegger.

The character of The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger was offered to me by Marcos Siega, who was one of our directors on The Terminal List. The Terminal List character’s efficiency and focus and dedication to his system probably put me in his mind when they were trying to cast Dexter . I love Marcos, and he brags now that he's the only guy to kill me twice. He directed the episode of Terminal List where Freddy Strain meets his heroic end. And then, of course Dexter always gets his at some point.

But when I first read the character, I just responded to how exact he was and how he liked to prolong the sensation and the torture of his victims — to the point where he's their reprieve from the madness he's induced upon them.

Yeah, the rearranging of household items just to drive people crazy is especially cruel. He was introduced in episode two with a highly effective Nine Inch Nails needle drop, “The Day the World Went Away.” We also saw how he uses online real estate listings to get the lay of the land before breaking into homes and observing his future victims as they sleep. The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger really illustrates the potential downside of having our homes listed on sites like Zillow, doesn't he? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Yeah, when we bought our house in L.A., we just drove around. It was better for us to do it the more personal, old-school way. So it’s an interesting tool he uses. He probably targets new homeowners. They haven't yet got their full security up and running, if he’s able to do these weekly home invasions and all of this foundational work for what is, in his mind, their ultimate release and then his release as well. He'd have to find very specific requirements for him to be able to achieve this.

But I quickly put all the logic away because if I was going to try to break it down that way, I would've shaved my face for the character. I would've worn a hair net. I would've tried, as much as I possibly could, not to leave any DNA around the scene. But Michael C. was the same. He had his moments where he was like, "I don't know, but it's a [show]. Let’s just do it.”

He lives a solitary life and believes relationships do more harm than good. How did you wrap your head around his philosophy that he's doing his victims and their surviving loved ones a favor by ending their relationships?

It’s tragic. ( Luna is interrupted by a Last of Us assistant with an update on the upcoming scene’s blocking. He then politely asks for his guitar to be retrieved from set. ) Sorry, we’re coming back from lunch.

I constructed this tragic backstory that he's in a bit of arrested development. He falls into that category of “hurt people hurt people” and probably underwent a lot of abuse by people who were supposed to be close to him and protect him. Then it just spiraled out of control into this new philosophy that any type of human interaction or connection is just a hindrance or an anchor or this curse and poison to one's life, and that he's the one to excise that poison. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As we were working it out, it manifested through these tempestuous, childlike knee-jerk reactions. He doesn't really talk to a lot of people or see a lot of people, so he’s lacking when it comes to understanding social contracts and connecting with people. When Dexter is trying to set him up and says, “You have a good share for Prater,” he quickly snaps back, “I know I have a good share.” It's almost like a child who's fighting with a step-sibling or something. But in my mind, it's all rooted in childhood, and that's how it manifests in his adult life. [ Writer’s Note: That petulant quality recurs when Dexter slices his cheek for his blood slide trophy. Instead of taking the pain like a tough guy, he reacts like a child. ]

How would you describe the experience of being Saran-wrapped to Dexter’s kill table?

Oh man. They told me that I'm probably in the upper tier of people who have spent the most time in the Saran wrap. I may have set a record somewhere along the line, I was told, partially because there's a whole scene of dialogue between Uma Thurman and Michael C. before Dexter and Sleepy get into their little tête-à-tête and he plunges his knife into his sternum.

But it did feel exciting. It's an iconic scenario and set. They give you modesty undergarments because you’re in your birthday suit on that slab. They Velcro you in, and then they use a staple gun to get it tight. So I was up there for a while, and I guess I’m impressed by my endurance in staying on the table. They feed you snacks and bring you a little sippy cup with a straw in it just so you're not too peckish or dehydrated up there. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

There's a great photo of my girl [next to me as I’m Saran-wrapped on Dexter’s kill table]. Like I said, she’s a big fan of the show, so she had me right where she wanted me. I joked that she could’ve asked for anything in that moment, and I would've been powerless against her.

The last time we spoke, you talked about attending the Schwarzenegger family's Christmas party in 2022. Arnold is also the father-in-law of The Terminal List star Chris Pratt. So did Chris cast you on The Terminal List in between Christmas carols at the Schwarzenegger estate?

( Laughs .) That's exactly what happened, although Arnold doesn't really have Christmas carols. He always has a mariachi band at his parties, which I've always loved. So this was the first Christmas dinner, post-COVID, [in 2022]. In prior years, he had big 250-person parties with whole petting zoos. He had a sanctuary of rescued wild animals, and they would bring animals over. All of the usual suspects were there: Dolph [Lundgren], Danny DeVito, Sly [Stallone[] and everybody.

But this time, we showed up for Christmas dinner together, and there were only 25 people there. I was really honored to be in that small family group. Katherine [Schwarzenegger] and Chris were sitting at our table, along with Conyers [Davis], Arnold's chief of staff, and his wife Elizabeth. Chris and I were just talking about life, football, music and where we come from, specifically my background in Texas.

Then I got to asking him about how The Terminal List was going, and he said, "If we're blessed to get a second season, there's a part that's perfect for you." That part, of course, was Freddy Strain. This was in 2022, and a lot of things happened from then until now. Between his busy schedule and the strike, there were numerous postponements to the second season getting going. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But when it did get going, it happened in a perfect window right after I finished Devil in Disguise . I was already in Toronto, and I took a two-month break for The Last of Us press tour. Then I was back to work in Toronto on The Terminal List . So that job started as a brotherly handshake in King Arnold's court.

Freddy is introduced as an old teammate of James Reece who now works for the CIA. More importantly, he's a family man who represents everything James used to be. I figured your character was safe just because the story needed that juxtaposition, but as soon as Freddy’s previously unseen family was shown on a video call, I knew the worst was about to happen. Was Freddy's death difficult for you to stomach?

You hit the nail on the head. I just saw a funny internet video where the characters who always get taken out in war films are the ones who are busy talking about their girl's picture in their wallet or their kids back home.

It’s a departure from what was in the novel, and the sniper duel is much more exciting in the way it's structured. It's really a beautiful tribute to the character and his ability. He's outmanned and outgunned, and he still puts up a hell of a fight. That day was very special, and a lot of heart and emotion was put into it.

Jared Shaw wrote it. He's a former team guy, a former Navy SEAL from SEAL Team 4, and he was one of my best friends on the shoot. In many ways, he's the inspiration for Freddy Strain. I remember him being there with me right before those moments, just supporting me and encouraging me and giving me both a literal and figurative pat on the back when it went well and everything felt right. You can see me in my head getting tuned up at one point, and he just placed his hand on my back and said, "You're doing beautiful, man. You got this." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was all about honoring the fallen in that episode and the early scenes of the finale. That's really the main focus and the main drive for all of it. We don't want to do dishonor to the men and women who serve, specifically the frogmen who we're trying to represent. [Freddy’s death] was the last day of the shoot, the absolute last day in Morocco, and it couldn't have been spent better.

Moving over to The Last of Us , Craig Mazin went solo between seasons two and three, with co-creator Neil Druckmann no longer actively involved in the show. Is everything business as usual as far as you're concerned?

Yeah, as far as it goes for me, I have a job to do. Bella and I are the longest-tenured people on this set, so we’re carrying the DNA of the story, Neil's intentions and his spirit forward. Craig loves the story that Neil has constructed, and he’s been a very stable steward who honors and maintains the source material. Craig loves his work, however hard it is. Every letter of every word of every script is written by Craig Mazin, so we just have a lot of well-earned belief and trust in him. And so we carry on.

We're doing our absolute best to bring the most explosive, most heart-wrenching culmination to what has been a really beautiful five years in my life. I just want to give the fans of the game and the fans of the show exactly what they deserve, which is, however morally ambiguous, a very explosive ending. It's what the piece deserves, and I'm excited to see everyone's reaction. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It's been massive, man. We've been going since last March, and we probably won't end until March, so it'll be a lot of time and effort dedicated to what has always been a one-of-a-kind story. Everyone is at the top of their game. So we're thankful for Craig, and I'm thankful for Bella and Kaitlyn [Dever]. They’re shouldering the massive weight of all this on their very slight shoulders, and I try my best, as Uncle Tommy, to offer what I can in support.

Is Pedro Pascal’s absence still felt on set?

Yeah, the spirit of Joel runs through everything. Pedro committed such an extraordinary performance to the screen, and you know the audience is certainly holding that flame for him. All the characters are too. In every action, in every life Tommy takes and in every round fired, there is that longing for his brother. I know Bella feels the same way about Ellie and the character’s grief. So, in the world of the show and in our memories of the great time we spent working together, we just carry him with us. But I always say Bella Ramsey is a great general, and we're in great hands with them at the helm.

Were you disappointed that you weren't around for Joel's death, as Tommy was in the games?

It was actually my suggestion. In the first season, I had discussed the idea with Craig and Neil. To have such a capable character walk in and be so quickly incapacitated — and to be helpless while these people take his brother from him — just didn't sit right. It was always something in the game that I questioned. Tommy would've had the situational awareness not to utter his brother's name to strangers, which he does in the game. He's the one who reveals Joel's identity. So I always lobbied and pitched the idea, What if Tommy isn't there? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid10' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I remember seeing Craig clock the idea, and I'd keep inquiring about it. Then, once he got into the writer's room for season two with Neil and [writer] Halley [Gross], Craig sent me a long, long text about what it would be now. And instead of helplessly being there as Joel is murdered, Tommy is back in Jackson fending off the horde of monsters as they breached the gates. He wrote literally everything you see on the screen in this big, long text. I was so excited and tortured and tormented for the following months to years, having to keep that all under my hat.

articles.title: GTA 6 - How to Make Money Early in the Game
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games As a wise man once said, "Cash rules everything around me." In Grand Theft Auto 6, that's more true than ever. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As a wise man once said, "Cash rules everything around me." In Grand Theft Auto 6 , that's more true than ever. While pulling off high-stakes robberies and filling your bank account has always been a primary objective throughout Grand Theft Auto's history, GTA 6 puts a much greater emphasis on money than ever before . Without it, you'll struggle to upgrade your car, buy new weapons, or even make your own version of Jason and Lucia look as fashionable as you want.

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6's story, you'll slowly unlock a number of new objectives that can allow you to yield greater money. In the early hours of the game, though, you'll find that you're pretty strapped for cash, as you struggle to obtain even a few thousand dollars at any given time. If you're looking to tuck away some money sooner rather than later, though, here are some tips to keep in mind as you begin your own adventure in Leonida.

In Chapter 1 of GTA 6 , you're solely controlling Jason as he works as a drug runner in the Leonida Keys. Many of the missions that Jason does for his boss, Brian, or with his cohort Donnie, will allow Jason to get some spending money. However, many of the game's biggest scores remain locked away, as you'll instead have to complete a number of missions to begin gaining access to this content.

Eventually, you'll reach a point where Jason will be able to go out and collect some drug drops that have been left in the bay. This, in addition to a handful of raids that you can take on against the Kingfishers, which are a local gang in the Keys, will be some of the best ways to quickly scrape together some money.

Perhaps the biggest downside to doing these tasks, however, is that the payouts you'll receive for these jobs are rather minimal. Brian and Donnie are the only two fences you'll have at your disposal in the first hours of GTA 6 , and each pays either a "Very Low" or "Low" rate for narcotics, jewelry, or marked bills that you're trying to sell. As such, even if you do go out of your way to complete a number of these odd jobs, the process of stacking paper to the ceiling will be a tough one.

Once you reach Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6 , you'll be able to start earning money at a much faster pace. Not only will you be able to begin holding up more local pawn shops and jewelry stores, but you'll also meet Moses, who is one of the game's most important characters when it comes to getting cash. Moses runs an auto shop and is also willing to purchase stolen vehicles for hundreds or thousands of dollars at once. As Lucia, you'll be able to begin hijacking cars and bringing them to Moses, which will allow you to get money faster than ever before in your BuckMe account.

The only problem with Moses is that he doesn't accept any and all vehicles at his shop. Any car that has a tracker on it will be a no-go for Moses, as that vehicle will be deemed too dangerous for him to purchase. Eventually, you'll be able to sell cars that have these trackers in place, but it won't be until a bit later on.

Even with this caveat in place, Moses is going to be your best option to collect money in the opening 10 or so hours of GTA 6 . As such, it's recommended that you prioritize knocking out many of the main missions in Chapter 1 early on so that you can more quickly begin living large as Jason and Lucia.

Grand Theft Auto 6 releases this week on November 19th for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. If you're looking to play the game earlier than this, there's a workaround that will allow you to jump in right now .

articles.title: Survivor's Fun Little Boat Ride With Christian Was Actually Rough For Production To Figure Out
articles.summary: Survivor looks way easier than it really is.
articles.content:
There are few reality TV shows with the legacy of Survivor , which is currently airing its whopping 51st season on CBS (and streaming with a Paramount+ subscription ). Apart from how much money Survivor players make , fans are also curious about how the various challenges come together. It turns out that Christian Chavez's boat ride from last week was actually a bit of a nightmare for production to figure out.

Talk about a logistical puzzle. Survivor is a huge production , but I never thought about how things like the tide and crew members made things even more complicated. It turns out that there was a very limited window where Christian could take the boat to the sandspit, and do the buoy challenge that would determine how many votes (if any) he'd have during the "double duo" week.

Well, my mind is spinning. As a longtime fan of the show, the difficulty of shooting the show is sometimes lost on me. After all, I'm usually more invested in the gameplay, and how well my Survivor draft picks are doing. There's so much that goes into each season's production that we never think of, which is why I appreciate Probst giving us these details about how it all comes together.

articles.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Will Never Get a 60fps Mode on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Players hoping to experience Grand Theft Auto 6 at 60 frames per second on current-generation consoles may need to adjust their expectations. Rockstar Games has made it clear that the highly anticipated open-world game is designed to run at 30fps on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and a future update isn't going to change […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Players hoping to experience Grand Theft Auto 6 at 60 frames per second on current-generation consoles may need to adjust their expectations. Rockstar Games has made it clear that the highly anticipated open-world game is designed to run at 30fps on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and a future update isn't going to change that. Even owners of Sony's more powerful PS5 Pro shouldn't expect a performance mode that doubles the game's frame rate.

As reported by IGN , Rockstar has confirmed that the PS5 Pro doesn't have the processing power necessary to run GTA 6 at 60fps. The console does offer a more capable graphics processor and improved upscaling technology compared to the standard PS5, but those advantages aren't enough to overcome the demands placed on its central processor. That limitation is particularly important for a game built around an enormous open world filled with complex systems and a densely populated environment.

The decision is consistent with Rockstar's previous confirmation that GTA 6 targets 30fps across current-generation consoles. The studio has emphasized that the game pushes the hardware to its limits, with its performance target allowing developers to maintain the level of environmental detail and activity they want throughout Leondia. Rather than offering separate graphics and performance options, Rockstar has built the console experience around a single presentation target, which makes sense considering the numerous of different configurations available even on just consoles.

The PS5 Pro's additional horsepower doesn't change the core limitation. While its upgraded GPU allows Rockstar to improve visual clarity details that aren't available on the standard PS5, its CPU is only modestly improved. This matters more than you may think, because running a game at 60fps requires the system to complete its work for each frame in roughly half the time available at 30fps.

This also means Xbox Series X|S owners shouldn't expect a different outcome. Rockstar's 30fps target applies across Microsoft's current console lineup, and neither the Series X nor the less powerful Series S has been positioned to offer a higher frame-rate option. There is no indication that a future patch will introduce one, either.

For players who prioritize smoother performance, the news will undoubtedly be disappointing, particularly given how much time has passed since the current console generation began. 30 FPS, especially after playing at a higher framerate, can be difficult to go back to. However, Rockstar appears committed to preserving the visual detail and complexity it has built into Grand Theft Auto 6 rather than compromising that experience to pursue a higher frame rate. Console players should therefore approach the November 19 release expecting 30fps, not a performance mode that might arrive soon after, or even later at all.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There were many thrilling moments and exciting updates in VisionQuest , but arguably the two biggest were the appearance of Billy Maximoff (and his reunion with Tommy and Vision) and the post-credits scene confirming that Wanda Maximoff is alive . Although Wanda has yet to reunite with her sons or Vision, and it's unclear when or if that will happen—although it currently feels much more likely than not—this is a major step towards the Maximoff family finally coming back together again, and it was also something many MCU fans had been waiting literal years for. However, this still didn't immediately mean a big happy family, either.

For one, the post-credits scene confirmed that Doctor Doom himself has come to collect Wanda, saying he will take the Scarlet Witch's power for himself, suggesting that Wanda may actually be a villain under Doom's control in Avengers: Doomsday . Additionally, though, Agatha All Along confirmed that Billy, who doesn't have most of his memories from the Hex beyond the existence of his brother, doesn't accept Wanda as his mom. In part, this is because he was raised by the Kaplans for about three years, and he therefore sees them as his parents, but it also revealed some seeming animosity for Wanda. That certainly rubbed fans the wrong way, but now, a blink-and-you-miss-it detail has suggested this major fan complaint may be a thing of the past.

When Billy appeared in VisionQuest , most of the attention was on this reunion, how emotional it was to see Tommy and Billy finally back together, and the moment in which Vision pulls Billy in for a hug. It was therefore very easy to miss the minor details on Billy's jacket, but eagle-eyed fans have now discovered that this jacket includes none other than the Scarlet Witch's crown. Already, that connection was there in light of the crown that appeared on Billy's head in Agatha All Along , but the fact that Billy drew this symbol onto his jacket himself means that he almost certainly has come around when it comes to how he feels about Wanda, and that's great news.

Wiccan has added Scarlet Witch’s crown to his jacket in ‘VISIONQUEST’ (via sarahyoung_costumedesign | IG) pic.twitter.com/m9XhoBR230

Hopefully, this easy-to-miss detail means that, once the family is finally reunited, Billy will be much more open to accepting Wanda as his mom. Already, audiences have seen signs of that change in Billy's overall feelings about the Maximoffs, given that he at first calls Vision "sir" and then is pulled into a hug. VisionQuest also concludes with Tommy and Vision headed to have dinner with Billy (and presumably Agatha as well ) in New Jersey. Yet, things are guaranteed to be more complicated with Wanda, especially given her current status with Doctor Doom, which means that, sadly, this fan-favorite MCU family is still far from a happy ending, if one is ever coming.

How do you think the Maximoffs will be reunited, and do you think it will happen in Doomsday ? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: Brad Pitt Wants To Make a Sequel to The 2025 Hit That Set His Own Box Office Record
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Apple Brad Pitt is currently out promoting The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, the highly anticipated sequel centering on his character from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Pitt won an Academy Award for portraying Cliff Booth, so it's exciting to see him take on the role again but it is not the only sequel he's […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Brad Pitt is currently out promoting The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the highly anticipated sequel centering on his character from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood . Pitt won an Academy Award for portraying Cliff Booth, so it's exciting to see him take on the role again but it is not the only sequel he's interested in making. That might come as a surprise to many because he's not an actor known for starring in a lot of sequels, but he has one on the horizon and announced that he wants to make one to 2025's hit film, F1 .

In the sports drama from director Joseph Kosinski, Pitt plays Sonny Hayes, a racer-for-hire who joins a struggling Formula One team in the hopes of turning it around. The movie became a monster hit , grossing over $600 million. That made it the highest-grossing film from Apple and of Pitt's legendary career. Given that level of success, it makes sense that Pitt would want to return to the role of Hayes and while promoting The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the actor discussed that filming for the long-awaited Ocean's 14 is set to start late next year, but he also gave an update on the future of F1 .

While being interviewed by Variety , Brad Pitt talked about Ocean's 14 before being asked if there was another movie he was interested in returning to. Without much hesitation, Pitt responded, "Yeah, yeah, actually. F1 ." The interviewer noted that the film is going to happen, as it was announced soon after the box office success of F1 was official that a sequel was being discussed. Apple had critical darlings like The Killers of the Flower Moon , but they hadn't released a major commercial hit to that point, so F1 was a welcome change.

Along with plans for a sequel, there was also talk of Apple turning F1 into an entire franchise. They could release several future film installments, maybe a TV show on their impressive streaming service (likely focusing on other racers rather than Hayes in that case), or even possibly branch out into the world of video games. In early 2026, the F1 sequel was officially greenlit. Apple understands that it has a legitimate hit with F1 , as fans of the sport, fans of sports films in general, and fans of Pitt will flock to see it.

Producer and F1 champion Lewis Hamilton mentioned how they wanted to take the time to ensure any further entries are as accurate as the original, so it might take a while to get one. As noted, F1 made history for Brad Pitt by becoming the highest-grossing film of his career. Looking at Hollywood's track record, sequels tend to perform better than the first installment; a follow-up to F1 would likely break that record. There's also a good chance that Ocean's 14 is a hit that grosses nearly as much, so Pitt has a lot to be excited about. If the F1 sequel is anywhere near as good as the first, Apple and Pitt have a special franchise on their hands.

What do you want to see from an F1 sequel? Let us know in the comments!

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man's Clone Saga will be the backbone of a new Marvel TV show for Prime Video, and this bizarre '90s comic book plot is about to get even weirder. When Spider-Noir premiered earlier this year and even earned Primetime Emmy recognition, it seemed like the streamer had a new franchise on their hands, which made […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man's Clone Saga will be the backbone of a new Marvel TV show for Prime Video, and this bizarre '90s comic book plot is about to get even weirder. When Spider-Noir premiered earlier this year and even earned Primetime Emmy recognition, it seemed like the streamer had a new franchise on their hands, which made the cancellation of the Nicolas Cage-led Marvel show a big surprise . It didn't take long for replacements to be revealed, though, with plans for multiple Spider-Man spinoffs confirmed to be in development at Prime Video.

One of those projects that seemed the closest to actually happening is a series that riffs on Spider-Man's Clone Saga, and now new details reveal how different it really will be. These details hail from Apocalyptic Horseman , a social media personality known for reporting scoops on upcoming projects. According to them, the film will follow Kaine and Ben Reilly, the same names as the Spider-Man clones from Marvel comics, only this time they'll be brothers on opposite sides of the law. Ben will be a cop, Kaine a criminal, and their relationship becomes more symbiotic after they gain spider-like superpowers that only work around each other.

The report goes on to reveal two additional details for the series, the first being that Miles Warren will be the main antagonist and that both Ben and Kaine will have to team up to solve a murder. That first reveal shouldn't surprise anyone who reads comics regularly, since Warren is the legal name of the Spider-Man antagonist The Jackal who is responsible for all those clones, but the second is interesting. Fresh off the heels of Lanterns taking the superhero genre in the direction of True Detective , it's easy to see how a pitch like this came together for Prime Video, especially after that DC series was a hit.

All the changes being made to the larger "Clone Saga" storyline are pretty bizarre anyway, and that's on top of the comic book plot being weird on its own. In the pages of Marvel comics, the '90s Clone Saga (technically the second with that name) has multiple Spider-Men operating at one time and at one point tried to pull the twist that Ben Reilly was the original person and Peter Parker was actually a clone of him. It all culminated in the reveal that Norman Osborn was alive and manipulating heroes and villains alike in his quest to torment Peter.

What these details about the show confirm, though, is that the same problems with Spider-Man spinoffs are going to persist well into the future. Even though details about the show confirm that elements of the comics are being used to bring it to life, the series will seemingly be totally separate from any larger Spider-Man mythology and may not even use the name "Spider-Man" in the slightest. Naturally the infinite reach of the "Spider-Verse" makes this feasible, but it has proven to be a problem before with the many Sony-made spinoff movies, and even Spider-Noir to an extent. Will Marvel fans flock to seeing a version of this beloved (but contrived) story on TV or is it doomed before it even gets started?

articles.title: The Batman's Robert Pattinson Is the New 007, So Now Is the Perfect Time to Discover James Bond's Wild Comic Book History
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Dymanite Entertainment We finally have a new James Bond and it's Edward. Oh, wait, wrong decade. Robert Pattinson, who is also playing Batman in The Batman series of movies, has been cast as the British spy. Pattinson has spent the years since his role in Twilight showing that he was more than a heart throb, taking a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google We finally have a new James Bond and it's Edward. Oh, wait, wrong decade. Robert Pattinson, who is also playing Batman in The Batman series of movies , has been cast as the British spy. Pattinson has spent the years since his role in Twilight showing that he was more than a heart throb, taking a variety of roles and showing his range. He's a serious actor who can play anything and after his excellent turn as Bruce Wayne, something no one expected out of him, him playing Bond is an exciting prospect. James Bond is an important part of pop culture and we've gone too long without a Bond movie. However, movies haven't been anywhere close to the only home of 007, as he's also starred in numerous comics over the decades.

James Bond was created by Ian Fleming, a character meant to play in the high stakes world of Cold War spies, and the character first appeared in the novel Casino Royale . Fleming ended up writing numerous Bond stories, they became movies, and that opened the floodgates. Licensed comics have been big business for years and Bond's history with comics goes back further than you think. With writer Grant Morrison about to write Bond comics and Pattinson's casting, it's a perfect time to ask M for the files on 007's missions in the world of the funny pages.

The first James Bond movie was Dr. No in 1962 and right away, James made his way to the comics. The movie was adapted in the United Kingdom in Classic Illustrated #158A, telling the film on the page. It would get reprinted in Europe by Dell Publishing in 1962, and then in the United States by DC Comics in 1963's Showcase #43. While the Bond movies were popular, the Dr. No adaptation didn't make as much of a splash and Bond comics were a thing of the past.

18 years later, Marvel Comics would try their hands at it with an adaptation of 1981's For Your Eyes Only . This one was popular, resulting in it being reprinted in a single magazine format and a collected edition. 1983 would see the House of Ideas publish an adaptation of Octopussy in magazine format, but it wasn't as big. However, there would be another long drought of Bond comics until 1989, when getting James Bond comics on a more regular basis became normal for a few years. The comic industry was in the midst of a boom, with numerous licensed comics popping up all over.

It started with an adaptation of License to Kill from Eclipse Comics, which was illustrated by Mike Grell, who was getting a lot of praise for his work on Green Arrow: The Longbow Hunters , and would lead to a both hardcover and paperback collected editions. Grell would have the distinction of being the first comic creator to write an original James Bond story, Permission to Die, which would be published over the course of two years from Eclipse.

GoldenEye was the big mid '90s Bond reboot and Topps Comics, the trading card company trying their hand at comics, would get the license to produce Bond stories. However, the second issue was delayed due to problems with its cover art, leading Topps to can the whole adaptation and scrap their plans for the license, which had included an all-new ongoing. However, the spy would have to wait no time at all for comics to come calling again. The mid '90s were also the time when Dark Horse Comics was putting out the best licensed comics around and they had their own deal.

See, the license to use a character and the license to adapt a movie can be separate. So, when other companies were making the adaptations, Dark Horse got the license to produce its own Bond stories in 1992. The company produced a number of Bond minis – Serpent's Tooth, Silent Armageddon, Light of My Death, Shattered Helix, Minute of Midnight , and The Quasimodo Gambit – between '92 and 1995. However, Bond comics never really seemed to catch on, leading Dark Horse to give up the license.

Bond comics would disappear for a while, with even the Casino Royale reboot not being adapted. The 2000s would go by with nary a Bond book to found. The '10s would dawn and still no Bond until 2014, when Dynamite Entertainment, who had been making a name for themselves with licensed comics (you might know them better as the publisher of The Boys ) acquired it. They decided to go in a different direction than others, by publishing stories set in two different timelines, focusing more on the literary version of the spy.

The first was set before his adventures in book Casino Royale and the second was more comtemporary, telling the stories of his adventures in the present day. It was an interesting way to approach the character, allowing creators to go a variety of directions with him. The first book, titled James Bond , premiered in 2015, and James Bond Origins would drop in 2018, with various miniseries and spin-offs getting published. The main series boasted talent like Warren Ellis, Kieron Gillen, Benjamin Percy, Andy Diggle, Jody Houser, Declan Shalvey, Garth Ennis, and more. The upcoming Grant Morrison reboot is just the latest in a long line of Bond comics.

The history of James Bond in the comic industry is an interesting one. There are few characters created outside comics who are better for comics than him, but it never really happened. One gets the impression that the Bond license is one that is tightly controlled by the owners, which made it hard to do anything but adaptations for a while. Bond is one of those characters who has become an indelible part of pop culture but honestly, it feels like the only times anyone has been serious about making comics starring the spy work was when Dark Horse had the license and then Dynamite.

Bond can be a tough sell in the 21st century. He's a character from a very specific time in history and he was tailor-made for it. It'll be interesting to see how Amazon handles the character; the Daniel Craig version went gritty, so maybe this time we'll get a more polished take. However, one of the best things about comics is the fact that you don't have to try to change the character to make him appeal to an audience that isn't into him. While the history of James Bond comics is one of starts and stops, I feel like we've finally reached the perfect era of comics for the character.

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of UGT / Fuzzy Door / MRC Ted is coming back to Peacock with a new animated series hitting later this December, and the first look at the new show has confirmed that two of the best characters from the live-action TV series are coming back. But there's still one major absence that fans have immediately noticed. Ted: The Animated Series is […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Ted is coming back to Peacock with a new animated series hitting later this December, and the first look at the new show has confirmed that two of the best characters from the live-action TV series are coming back. But there's still one major absence that fans have immediately noticed. Ted: The Animated Series is a new entry in the wider Ted franchise that picks up 12 years after the events of the feature films , and reintroduces the older John and Ted as they raise their families together.

But with the success of the Ted TV series with Peacock, fans had gotten attached to those earlier depictions of the franchise's characters . This is especially true for the members of the Bennett family, and thankfully it's been confirmed that Matty and Susan are set to return to the new animated series with Scott Grimes and Alanna Ubach likely reprising their roles. You can check out the first look at them below, but Giorgia Whigham's Blaire unfortunately seems unaccounted for right now.

Ted: The Animated Series is set back in the canon of the Ted films, and that means Mark Wahlberg returns as the older version of John for the occasion. The Ted TV series technically was in line with the films, but had taken on a whole life of its own with fans online especially with the different iterations of Matty and Susan Bennett. The TV series had fully invented new versions of John's parents (who had been portrayed by Ralph Garman and Alex Bortstein in the first Ted film, and even had different names), so it's a great sign to see them folded into the animated series.

But their return also raises a few questions. It's likely that Ted: The Animated Series isn't too concerned with having a tight timeline of events, but Matty and Susan should technically be in the eighties by this point given that they were already a bit older in the 1990s. And through the first trailer, Blaire doesn't seem to appear either. She was the standout brand new addition to the formula in the TV series, so there's a hope that she makes a surprise appearance as an older version of herself in one of these animated series episodes to come.

Ted: The Animated Series will be making its debut with Peacock on Thursday, December 17th with eight episodes all available at once. Additional episodes of the animated series planned for a release sometime in 2027, but no concrete release date has been announced as of this time. The core cast of the films are returning to reprise their respective roles with Seth MacFarlane as Ted, Mark Wahlberg as John, Amanda Seyfried as Sam, and Jessica Barth as Tami-Lynn all set alongside new additions Kyle Mooney as Apollo and Liz Richman as Ruth.

With the Ted franchise continuing its story through the animated series, it unfortunately means that the live-action TV series is likely not going to return anytime soon. Seth MacFarlane noted that while the production team and Peacock had deemed the series a success, it was just "too expensive" to keep producing . So it seems like this animated series might be the only way forward for now. How do you feel about Matty and Susan returning in Ted: The Animated Series without Blaire? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: The Internet Can’t Stop Talking About People’s Mouths In Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. I Can’t Unsee It
articles.summary: If you haven't watched this yet, give it two minutes. You can't unsee it.
articles.content:
I’m pretty good about keeping an eye on the Christmas movies schedule , but I was a few days late to Netflix’s The Christmas Switch . (Can you blame a girl when Hallmark is over here dropping holiday time loop bangers ?) The new romantic holiday comedy was written and filmed in Sweden, but you’d seemingly never know it from the English version, which is dubbed over in English, and has the actors’ mouths matching the English words, as well. Let's talk about this strange magic.

It was uncanny. It made the viewing experience weird. I didn’t particularly like it. And it turned a perfectly OK holiday film into something far stranger.

The Christmas Switch was made available for anyone with a Netflix subscription on November 12th, so it's been around for a few days. It’s currently in the Top 10 in the US, along with fellow Christmas flicks The Gospel of Christmas and A Dog’s Perfect Christmas . So, it’s safe to say a lot of people have witnessed this mouth edit phenomenon.

Listen, we all know dubbing is annoying in general. I’ve watched every season of the now-canceled Maxton Hall on Amazon Prime Video, and I don’t like the mouths not matching the English language version, either. Still, at least that feels authentic. And there’s always the option to watch just with subtitles. (This is true for The Christmas Switch too; it’s just not the option that comes up on English-language Netflix first.)
